$schema_note: Specification of the Gentics CMS MCP tool surface (cms-mcp). Companion document: stage1/04-mcp-scope.md. Every inputSchema and outputSchema is JSON Schema draft 2020-12. $ref values resolve against the root of THIS document; dereference them before handing a schema to an MCP client. Tool names are snake_case; input and output field names are camelCase, identical to the CMS REST model names. Input schemas are strict (additionalProperties false); output schemas are intentionally open so cms-mcp can add fields additively.

changelog.summary: Initial tool surface: 50 tools in 7 groups, with strict input schemas, CMS endpoint mapping per tool and scenario coverage for S1 to S4.

Authentication reduced to a bearer CMS API token the client presents; auth vocabulary aligned with the GenAIx API; endpoint path recorded in the transport block; transport implementation state and the OAuth 2.1 extension added; mandatory query wrapping recorded as a MUST on the three search tools.

Documentation separated: this file describes the CMS MCP server only, with client-side integration moved to the integration guide, and the correlation headers described generically as headers a client may send. Implementation model added: one annotation scanned at start-up, with every tool marked generated or composite, and per-tool CMS permission requirements. Construct authoring gained list_part_types, list_datasources and get_datasource, and the part type id became an integer validated against an installation-level allowlist instead of a fixed enum. Search tools trimmed: search_content and count_content keep only the inputs the scenarios use, highlighting is always on, hits carry a reference and selection metadata rather than an embedded object, and count_content groups one way at a time.
/mcp decided; field names camelCase matching the REST models.
changelog.detail: The endpoint path is settled at {cms_base_url}/mcp, since the MCP server is its own servlet rather than part of the Jersey REST servlet; the consequence that the servlet must authenticate bearer CMS API tokens itself, being outside the /rest/* filter chain, is kept as a requirement. Every tool input and output field name, nested fields included, is now camelCase and identical to the CMS REST model name, so the module needs no naming transformation; tool names stay snake_case and the GenAIx API keeps its own snake_case.

changelog.detail: The tool list, groups, input and output schemas, permissions and the transport section stand as agreed. A change from here is made by agreement between the parties and recorded in this changelog, with a breaking change only where no additive form exists; 1.0.0 follows at the demo-readiness checkpoint.

changelog.summary: Agreed by all parties. Findings from the first GenAIx implementation against rc.1: five input schemas made client-safe, per-tool listing, list_templates in phase one, the part-reference spelling, the gate correlation header, and clarified semantics. No tool renamed or removed.
changelog.detail: (1) get_construct, update_construct, add_page_tag, add_construct_to_package and find_similar expressed 'exactly one of two identifying members' as a root-level anyOf in inputSchema; MCP hosts that convert tool schemas for a model reject or drop such a root, so the tools never reached the model. The alternation moved out of the schema into the new tool-level inputRule {exactlyOne: [...]} plus the description, and the server enforces it (invalid-params). (2) tools/list is computed per tool, not per group: a tool is listed when the acting user's type-level CMS permissions can satisfy its permissions entry, so a content creator sees the read tools of the constructs group (list_constructs, get_construct, list_part_types, list_construct_categories, list_datasources, get_datasource) without holding updateconstructs. Group roles are a summary of the tools' roles. Read-only allowlists (quality gates, reviewer agents) may name a group's read tools by access, never its writes. (3) list_templates is phase one, folder- or node-scoped, in content_read with role any: a content creation flow must be able to offer the templates a folder allows. (4) handlebarsTemplate and parts[].keyword state the one spelling the CMS Handlebars part type resolves, cms.tag.parts.<keyword>; the earlier tag.parts.<keyword> does not render. (5) New optional correlation header X-GenAIx-Gate for calls a quality gate or reviewer agent makes; whoami is required of every server that authenticates the transport (it is how a client verifies a credential); initialize is authenticated like every other request, so an unauthenticated probe sees only the 401. (6) count_content counts over the same indexed fields and object types search_content matches, so a count reproduces a search's total when called with the search's own inputs; queryUsed is informative and cannot be replayed. (7) ObjectRef.url is the page's preview or published URL, niceUrl its public path, path its folder path; a client that needs one link takes url, then niceUrl, then path. (8) No tool submits a page for review: publish_page queues the page for approval when the user lacks publishpages, and a review request by a user who may publish is handled on the client side. (9) idempotencyKey, transport and everything else unchanged.

transport.url_note: Decided by the CMS team. The MCP server is its own servlet, not part of the Jersey REST servlet, so it is mounted on the servlet context at /mcp and not under /rest. The mapping is an exact path rather than a prefix, because the SDK transport checks requestURI.endsWith(mcpEndpoint) and answers 404 otherwise. The path stays configurable through MCP_PATH, normalised to start with / and to have no trailing /, so an installation can move it; a client therefore uses the endpoint its installation is configured with rather than deriving a URL from cms_base_url. Because /mcp sits outside the /rest/* filter chain, the MCP servlet cannot inherit the CMS session filter and must authenticate bearer CMS API tokens itself; see implementation_state.blocking_gap.
transport.stateless_note: The SDK transport issues an Mcp-Session-Id response header and manages its own transport sessions. Stateless here means no CMS authorization state and no conversational state is bound to that id: every request is independently authenticated from its bearer token, so a client may reconnect freely.

server_info.name: Gentics CMS
server_info.instructions: MCP server of a Gentics CMS instance. It provides access to the CMS REST API.

implementation_state.status: Draft transport implemented and mounted on the decided path /mcp; no tools registered yet.
implementation_state.scope: The CMS MCP servlet draft is functional at the protocol level (initialize, capability negotiation, session handling) and the endpoint path is settled. The names and structures below describe that draft; they are the current shape of the transport rather than a frozen contract.

sdk.why_not_bundle: The io.modelcontextprotocol.sdk:mcp convenience bundle pulls Jackson 3 (tools.jackson.*) while the CMS uses Jackson 2.21.x, so the bundle would put two Jackson stacks into the shaded server jar.

implementation_state.mounted_by: com.gentics.contentnode.server.OSSRunner.addMcpServlet, with ServletHolder.setAsyncSupported(true), which is mandatory because the transport calls request.startAsync() for SSE streams
implementation_state.registration_hook: MCPServer.getServer() returns Optional<McpSyncServer>; tools are registered on it
implementation_state.servlet_namespace: Jetty 12 ee10, jakarta.servlet (Servlet 6.0). The SDK is compiled against Servlet 6.1 but its servlet transports use only 6.0 API, so the CMS stack is compatible as it stands.

config.note: The decided path. Configurable so an installation can move the endpoint, not an invitation to change the contract.

remaining_work: Authenticate the endpoint, as set out in blocking_gap below.
Register the tools on the McpSyncServer instance, driven from the resource annotations.
Expose the CMS resources as MCP tools through those annotations, which is the goal the draft prepares for.

blocking_gap.what: The MCP endpoint is currently UNAUTHENTICATED. The CMS session filter is mapped only to /rest/*, and the MCP servlet is mounted outside that chain at /mcp, so no filter in the REST stack can authenticate it. Bearer authentication against CMS API tokens must therefore be wired into the MCP servlet itself.
requirements: Accept Authorization: Bearer <CMS API token> at /mcp and resolve it to a CMS user inside the MCP servlet, through the transport's contextExtractor (McpTransportContextExtractor<HttpServletRequest>), which can hand the resolved CMS session down into the tool handlers. This is the servlet's own work: /mcp is outside the /rest/* filter chain.
Reject an unauthenticated or unresolvable request with HTTP 401 before the MCP envelope; no anonymous access to any tool, and no fallback to a service identity.
Validate the Origin header with a ServerTransportSecurityValidator (the SDK default is NOOP), since the CMS is browser facing.
Run each tool call in a transaction owned by the resolved user, so CMS permissions, locks and audit attribution apply unchanged.

auth.description: A named CMS API token belonging to the acting human user. There is no service account and no installation-wide CMS credential. A user, or a client acting with that user's CMS session, creates a named token through POST /rest/admin/token and the client then presents it on every MCP request; cms-mcp sees only the bearer token and has nothing to provision, look up or negotiate. A client can confirm a token belongs to the user it expects by calling whoami. Deleting the token in the CMS makes the next request answer 401. How a multi-user host stores such tokens per user is an integration concern, not part of this contract. Every request, initialize included, is authenticated: an unauthenticated client sees the 401 and nothing of the server, so a reachability probe without a credential learns only that the endpoint answers. whoami is therefore required of this server (it is the call a client uses to verify a credential it holds).

future_oauth2.what: The MCP Authorization specification models exactly one authorization path and it is not a static token: the MCP server is an OAuth 2.1 resource server, the authorization server is a separate role, discovery runs through RFC 9728 protected resource metadata, and RFC 8707 resource indicators bind a token to one server. cms-mcp implements none of it, so Phase One uses a static bearer token the client presents.

spec_revisions.note: First authorization spec: 401 then OAuth 2.1 authorization code with PKCE, authorization server assumed to live at the MCP server's own root. OAuth 2.1 draft-12, RFC 8414, RFC 7591. No protected resource metadata, no resource indicators.

Major rewrite and the revision most hosts implement today. MCP server becomes an OAuth 2.1 resource server; RFC 9728 protected resource metadata MUST; RFC 8707 resource indicators MUST; audience validation MUST; token passthrough forbidden.
Interim revision, no longer indexed separately on the public spec site, but real: it is what the MCP Java SDK's conformance runs target.

Current. Carries 2025-06-18 forward and adds RFC 6750 cited explicitly, RFC 9207 iss validation against mix-up attacks, Client ID Metadata Documents as the preferred registration route with dynamic client registration deprecated, dual discovery across RFC 8414 and OpenID Connect Discovery, and a formal 403 insufficient_scope step-up flow.

cms_would_need: Serve GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource (RFC 9728) whose authorization_servers array names at least one authorization server. The CMS need not BE the authorization server; it can name an existing identity provider such as Keycloak.

Answer 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="https://<cms>/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource", optionally with a scope hint. Clients are required to parse that header, so this is what makes the bare 401 actionable.

Validate the access token's audience against its own canonical resource URI on every request (RFC 8707 section 2). A valid token from a trusted issuer is not enough: it must have been minted for this resource.
Never pass the received token through to any upstream API; obtain a separate credential instead. This is the confused-deputy mitigation and it is normative.
Answer 403 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="insufficient_scope", scope=..., resource_metadata=... so a compliant client can step up instead of failing.
Optionally accept Client ID Metadata Document URLs as client_id, or support RFC 7591 dynamic client registration, for onboarding without per-client pre-registration.
future_oauth2.why_not_phase_one: Audience validation is what makes a CMS API token inadmissible in the strict model, since such a token is not audience-bound. The specification never names static tokens or API keys as an alternative scheme; a static token is simply a bearer token obtained out of band, skipping discovery, registration, PKCE and resource binding. It is a workable Phase One mechanism but should be read as a gap against the specification rather than a design.
future_oauth2.java_sdk_gap: The MCP Java SDK ships NO built-in authorization by deliberate design. It exposes pluggable hooks at the server transport layer (the same contextExtractor seam the Phase One bearer requirement uses) and leaves the mechanism to the host framework. First-party OAuth and API-key support lives in Spring AI MCP Security, and the SDK reports its authorization conformance as "Auth (Spring)". That route does not fit the CMS, which is a Jetty 12 and Jersey application rather than a Spring one, so resource-server support would be custom servlet or transport work: a real estimate, not a dependency upgrade.
future_oauth2.no_tool_impact: Authorization is a transport concern: no tool in this file changes when the CMS moves from a static bearer token to OAuth 2.1.
future_oauth2.source: MCP Authorization specification revisions 2025-03-26, 2025-06-18 and 2026-07-28, and the MCP Java SDK documentation.
future_oauth2.request_to: A requirement towards the CMS implementation; see 04-mcp-scope.md section 2.2.1 and section 10.

token_endpoints.note: Creates a token for the currently authenticated user from {name, expires, pruneOnExpiry} and returns the secret once. A client that stores a token per user should use a predictable token name so a later registration can find and replace it. An agent host instead creates one short-lived token per workflow session, so this endpoint is called often and cms-mcp sees many short-lived tokens per user.

request_fields.name: The token label, and the only marker a client has; there is no purpose field. An agent host names a session token genaix-<session id>.
request_fields.expires: Unix timestamp in seconds at which the token stops working. 0 means never; a past value is rejected; the token is valid only while expires > now, so expiry is evaluated per call.
request_fields.pruneOnExpiry: When true the CMS deletes the token row once it expires, instead of leaving a dead row behind.

token_endpoints.note: Lists the current user's tokens, which is how a client finds and replaces a stale token of its own name. To be confirmed: whether the response exposes the token name.
Deletes one of the current user's tokens; 404 when it is not theirs. Revocation here makes the next MCP call answer 401.

auth.token_endpoints_source: AdminResource in cms-restapi. The CMS API token endpoints are available on a CMS development build, where the creation request is {name, expires, pruneOnExpiry}. The model classes in com.gentics.contentnode.rest.model.token are not yet published, and whether GET /rest/admin/token exposes the token name still has to be confirmed.
auth.session_mode: A username and password login returns a session cookie, which session-mode REST clients send on every request; that is how a client authenticates to /rest/admin/token in order to create a token. cms-mcp clients use bearer tokens, not session mode.
auth.failure: HTTP 401 before the MCP envelope, so a client can tell a failed tool from a lost credential without parsing a tool result.

headers.name: X-GenAIx-Session
headers.description: Optional correlation header: identifier of the calling client's conversation or task. Opaque to the server, logged verbatim, never a source of authorisation.

headers.name: X-GenAIx-Run
headers.description: Optional correlation header: identifier of the individual agent run, the unit a user can cancel. Opaque to the server, logged verbatim.

headers.name: X-GenAIx-Client
headers.description: Optional client identifier and version, for example somehost/1.4.2.

headers.name: X-GenAIx-Gate
headers.description: Optional correlation header: identifier of the quality gate or reviewer agent making the call on the user's behalf. Sent instead of, or next to, X-GenAIx-Run when the call belongs to a gate rather than to the agent's own run. Opaque to the server, logged verbatim, never a source of authorisation.

transport.headers_note: These three are optional and a server must not reject a request that omits them. Their names are fixed by this contract so that one log format works for every client, letting a client's own log and the CMS access log be joined after the fact.

dynamic_tool_listing.description: tools/list is computed per request and per tool from the acting user's type-level CMS permissions: a tool is listed when the user's permissions can satisfy the tool's permissions entry, and omitted otherwise. In effect a whole group disappears when none of its tools can be used (admin without createuser/updategroupuser, content_write without page create or edit permission in any node, search when the CMS feature elasticsearch is inactive), while a group with mixed access lists only what the user may call: a content creator sees the read tools of constructs without holding updateconstructs. Per-object checks still happen on the call and surface as permission-denied.
dynamic_tool_listing.clients_must: Tolerate the list changing between calls and intersect it with their own allowlist.

error_mapping.note: Transport-level 401, no MCP envelope, so a client sees a connection failure rather than a tool error.
The acting user lacks the right, not the calling client.
Another user holds the edit lock; detail names them.
Only from POST /rest/elastic/*: CMS feature elasticsearch is not activated. Documented in the @StatusCodes annotation on cms-search-api SearchResource.
Reserved. The CMS has no rate limiter today.

conventions.result: Every tool returns structuredContent matching its outputSchema plus one text block of at most ~400 characters summarising the outcome in words.
conventions.naming: Tool names are snake_case. Input and output field names are camelCase and identical to the CMS REST model names: nodeId, folderId, pageId, templateId, constructId, datasourceId, typeId, niceUrl, editedAfter, groupBy, groupLimit, markupLanguage. group is metadata, not a name prefix.
conventions.idempotency: Desired-state write tools are idempotent. create_page, add_page_tag, create_user and create_construct are not and carry a guard. Every write tool accepts an opaque idempotencyKey, logged but not yet enforced.
conventions.bulk: No bulk writes: one object per write call, so the audit trail stays one line per object.
conventions.ref_resolution: $ref values resolve against the root of this document (#/definitions/...). Dereference them before handing a schema to an MCP client.

implementation_model.mechanism: One annotation on a Java method, scanned at start-up: @McpTool(name, group, access, permissions).

annotation_attributes.name: The MCP tool name, snake_case, unique across the server.
annotation_attributes.group: The tool group, used for allowlisting and for the coarse tools/list filter.
annotation_attributes.permissions: The CMS permission requirements a caller must hold, as object type plus permission bits, expressed in the CMS's existing permission vocabulary (the perm resource types and the PermHandler privileges). Roles and groups are created dynamically in a CMS installation, so the annotation never names a role or a group.

naming.rule: Tool input and output field names are camelCase and identical to the CMS REST model names, nested fields included. Tool names stay snake_case.
naming.no_transformation: The module performs no naming transformation. A generated tool's input schema comes from the annotated parameters and the Jackson models the REST resource already uses, and its output schema from the return type the same way, so the names an agent sends are the names the CMS declares. Composite tool DTOs are written in the same style, so both kinds look alike from outside.
naming.why: A translation layer is code to maintain, test and keep in step with every REST model change, and it makes each validation message, log line and JavaDoc reference a name that does not exist on the other side. Reusing the REST names removes the layer and the drift with it.
naming.genaix_api: The GenAIx API keeps its own snake_case field names. Nothing crosses the boundary field by field: tool arguments travel as opaque JSON shaped by the tool schema, so the two conventions never have to meet.

scanner_derives: the tool name, group, access and permission requirements, from the annotation
the LLM-facing description, from the method JavaDoc including @param text per field
the input schema, from the parameter DTO through the Jackson model already used for REST, which is why the field names are the REST field names
the output schema, from the return type the same way
the tools/list filter, from access and the declared permission requirements
the audit line: name, group, access and the object references the call touched

permission_evaluation.listing: tools/list hides a tool when the acting user's effective permissions, resolved from their groups and roles, can never satisfy the tool's declared requirements. This is a capability check, not an object check: a user who may edit pages somewhere still sees the page write tools.
permission_evaluation.call: Every call re-checks the declared requirements against the concrete target object inside the transaction, which is the check that actually protects the object. A user who sees a tool may still be refused on a particular page, folder or node, and that refusal is a permission-denied problem.
permission_evaluation.why_both: The listing check keeps a capability the user does not have out of the model's toolbox; the call check is the authority. Neither replaces the other.

planning_metadata.roles: The roles values on each tool and the roles list at the top of this file are planning metadata of this specification: suggested role profiles a CMS administrator may map to groups. They are not annotation input and the CMS does not generate them.
planning_metadata.scenarios: The scenarios values are planning metadata of this specification, used to prove that the showcase scenarios are covered. They are not part of the annotation and the CMS does not generate them.

kinds.generated: The annotation sits on an existing REST resource method and the tool is a one-to-one mapping. No new code and no separate schema to maintain: the tool exists because the method does.
kinds.composite: An ordinary method in the cms-mcp module carrying the same annotation, whose body calls two or three resource implementations inside one transaction with the user context from the bearer token. Used where a single REST call cannot express what an agent needs to do safely.

implementation_model.why_composites: A composite is Java inside the CMS build, so a changed resource signature stops it compiling and someone fixes it before the build passes. A generated tool fails the other way: the method still compiles, the scanner still produces a schema, and the schema silently changes shape, so an agent sends what worked yesterday and gets a validation error at run time or a silently ignored field. Compile-time breakage inside the CMS build is cheaper than silent runtime drift.
rules: Expose the primitives next to every composite, so an agent can fall back to the underlying operations. The one exception is the raw Elasticsearch passthrough, which must never be exposed unwrapped.

This file is the contract. A test in the CMS build compares the generated tool list against it on names, groups, access, required input fields and declared permission requirements, and fails the build on a difference. A client mirrors that check by comparing tools/list against the allowlist its workflow declares, and marks the workflow unavailable on a mismatch rather than discovering the gap mid-run.

Changes are additive once tools ship. New tools, new optional input fields and new output fields are free; renaming a tool or a field, removing one, or narrowing an input is breaking and bumps the tool specification version.
implementation_model.conformance_test: Both sides run the same comparison. In the CMS build: scan the annotations, generate the tool list, and assert that every tool in this file is present with the same group, access, required input fields and permission requirements, and that no tool is exposed that this file does not describe. Roles and scenarios are not compared, because the CMS does not generate them. On the client side: fetch tools/list at session start, intersect it with the workflow allowlist, and fail closed when a required tool is missing.
implementation_model.per_tool_fields: Every tool carries implementation: {kind: generated} or {kind: composite, composes, transaction}, and permissions: the object type and permission bits a caller must hold. search_content additionally carries never_exposed_unwrapped: true.

responsibilities.cms_team: module package: servlet mounting, transport, request authentication against CMS API tokens, transaction and permission context, REST extensions and Elasticsearch mapping additions a tool needs
responsibilities.ioflair: the tools inside the module: @McpTool annotations on resource methods (generated tools) and the composite tool methods; this specification

groups.title: Identity and permissions
groups.description: Who the acting user is, which nodes they see, and what they may do. Needed by every scenario and available to every authenticated user.

tools.name: whoami
tools.title: Who am I
tools.description: Returns the CMS user this session acts as, with their groups. Call this once at the start of any task so you can address the user correctly and know which groups bound your permissions. Do NOT use it to decide whether an action is allowed: group membership does not tell you object permissions, use get_permissions for that.

composes: the group list, reduced to the fields an agent needs

cms.notes: GET /user/me?groups=true returns UserLoadResponse {user: User}; User = {id, firstName, lastName, description, email, login, groups: Group[]}. The password field of User is never returned by this tool. A client that stores a token per user should also call this to confirm the token resolves to the user it expects.

tools.name: get_permissions
tools.title: Get effective permissions
tools.description: Returns the acting user's effective permissions on one CMS object, or on a whole object type, as named booleans. Call this before proposing any write, and before telling the user an action is possible. Do NOT use it to enumerate what other users may do, that is get_group_permissions, and do NOT treat a granted flag on a type as permission on every instance of that type.

composes: decoding the perm and rolePerm bit strings into a named boolean map

permissions.description: Optional narrowing. Omit to get the full decoded map.

granted.description: Decoded named permissions, e.g. {view: true, edit: true, publish: false}.

cms.notes: PermBitsResponse carries perm and rolePerm as raw bit strings plus privilegeMap {privileges: {name: boolean}, languages: [LanguagePrivileges]}. cms-mcp MUST decode into the named map and SHOULD NOT expose the bit strings to the model; they are kept in the output only for human debugging. GET /perm/{perm}/{type}/{id} returns PermResponse {granted} for a single check.

tools.name: list_nodes
tools.title: List nodes
tools.description: Lists the nodes (sites and channels) the acting user can see, with their languages and default media folders. Use it to resolve a node by name and to learn which languages a node supports before creating or translating a page. Do NOT use it to browse content, use get_folder_tree.

cms.notes: GET /node returns NodeList with q, sort, page, pageSize, perms. Languages come from GET /node/{id}/languages; cms-mcp may fold them in per node or fetch them lazily.

groups.title: Content retrieval (Content RAG)
groups.description: Permission-filtered retrieval over the CMS Elasticsearch indices, plus relational reverse lookups. The CMS injects every permission and scope filter server-side.

tools.name: search_content
tools.title: Search content
tools.description: The one retrieval tool for CMS content. Searches the Elasticsearch indices for pages, folders, files, images and forms the acting user may see, and returns references with highlight snippets. TWO-STEP PATTERN: this tool finds candidates, it does not give you their content. Call get_page (or get_file, get_image) on a hit before quoting it, summarising it or asserting anything about its wording. CORPUS LIMIT: for pages the indexed text is only what an editor typed into a text part, as separate values, for the current version. Text that comes from the template, from navigation or from rendering is NOT indexed, so a miss does not mean the published page lacks the phrase. The total is filtered by the user's permission groups but not by per-object permission, so treat it as an upper bound and count the hits you actually received when the number matters. Do NOT use this tool to list a folder (use list_folder_items), to count without reading (use count_content) or to find duplicates of a known object (use find_similar).

composes: query construction from the structured input
implementation.note: The raw Elasticsearch passthrough must never be exposed as a tool of its own: a body without query.bool reaches Elasticsearch with no CMS permission filter, so the wrapped search tools are the only search surface.

permissions.scope: every hit, enforced server-side by the passthrough filter

query.description: Natural language or Lucene query_string syntax, matched over the name, description, path and indexed text of the object.

recursive.description: Include subfolders of folderId. Ignored when folderId is absent.

languages.description: Language codes. Narrows which per-language indices are searched.

online.description: True for published objects only, false for offline only. Omit for both.

templateIds.description: Restrict to pages built on these templates.

editedAfter.description: Only objects edited at or after this Unix timestamp.

filters.description: The three supported filters, AND-combined and translated into bool.filter term and range clauses. Anything else has to be expressed through rawQuery.

rawQuery.description: Escape hatch: a full Elasticsearch query DSL body, used instead of query and filters. The server rewrites it into a bool query so the CMS injects its permission, node, folder and wastebin filters, so it cannot widen access, and a body that cannot be wrapped is rejected rather than sent unfiltered. Report queryUsed to the user whenever you use it.

totalIsExact.description: False whenever the total is a permission-group upper bound.

snippets.description: Highlight fragments, one per matched text value. Highlighting is always on.

items.description: A reference plus enough metadata to choose, and nothing more. Call get_page for content.

queryUsed.description: The Elasticsearch body actually sent, for transparency.

cms.notes: Non-OSS cms-search module, cms-search-api SearchResource: POST /elastic/{type}/_search with type in page|folder|file|image|form (IndexType enum) and a raw ES DSL body. Query parameters come from SearchParameterBean: nodeId (single int), folderId (repeatable int), recursive, language (repeatable, NOT languages), wastebin (exclude|include|only, left at exclude by this tool). SearchResourceImpl.addFilters injects a terms filter on the user's groupId values (from PermHandler.getGroupIds(nodeId)), a nodeId term, a folderId terms filter and the deleted term into query.bool.filter, and the hit loop post-filters every hit with Transaction.canView. cms-mcp MUST NOT re-implement that filtering. MANDATORY QUERY WRAPPING: cms-mcp MUST send every body to /rest/elastic shaped as {"query":{"bool":{"must":[<the actual query>],"filter":[]}}}, and MUST wrap a caller-supplied rawQuery the same way when it does not already carry query.bool. SearchResourceImpl.addFilters returns the body UNMODIFIED on three paths: no query key at all (so a bare {"size":0,"aggs":{...}} body is never filtered), a query without a bool key (the source carries a "// TODO add bool?" comment at that branch), and a bool.filter that is neither an object nor an array. On any of those paths NONE of the groupId terms filter, nodeId filter, folderId filter or wastebin filter is applied and only the per-hit canView post-filter remains. to be confirmed: Gentics should harden addFilters to create the bool wrapper itself and to fail closed, so correctness does not depend on every client shaping its body correctly. COUNT ACCURACY: the per-hit post-filter replaces hits.hits only and does NOT adjust hits.total, and aggregations are not post-filtered at all. Totals and aggregation counts therefore reflect the injected group-based filter, not the per-object canView check, and may overstate slightly where group permission and object permission diverge. Highlighting is always requested, on the indexed text and description fields, three fragments of 200 characters. The hit's _object attribute is deliberately NOT passed through: a client reads content with get_page instead, which keeps the result small and makes the verification step explicit. Answers HTTP 405 when the CMS feature elasticsearch is inactive.

tools.name: find_similar
tools.title: Find similar objects
tools.description: Finds objects similar to a given object or to a block of text, for duplicate detection before creating a page and for checking whether a construct like the one you are about to build already exists. Pass exactly one of ref or text; a call with neither or both is refused as invalid-params. Do NOT use it for keyword search with filters, that is search_content.

composes: a more_like_this clause built from a ref or a text block

permissions.scope: every hit, enforced server-side by the passthrough filter

inputRule.note: Exactly one of these members must be present. Enforced by the server with invalid-params; kept out of inputSchema because a root-level anyOf/oneOf is not accepted by every MCP host that hands tool schemas to a model.

cms.notes: A more_like_this query over name, description and content. With ref, cms-mcp builds the more_like_this like clause from the indexed document (_index plus _id); with text it passes the text directly. The more_like_this clause goes into query.bool.must, never at the top of query: MANDATORY QUERY WRAPPING: cms-mcp MUST send every body to /rest/elastic shaped as {"query":{"bool":{"must":[<the actual query>],"filter":[]}}}, and MUST wrap a caller-supplied rawQuery the same way when it does not already carry query.bool. SearchResourceImpl.addFilters returns the body UNMODIFIED on three paths: no query key at all (so a bare {"size":0,"aggs":{...}} body is never filtered), a query without a bool key (the source carries a "// TODO add bool?" comment at that branch), and a bool.filter that is neither an object nor an array. On any of those paths NONE of the groupId terms filter, nodeId filter, folderId filter or wastebin filter is applied and only the per-hit canView post-filter remains. to be confirmed: Gentics should harden addFilters to create the bool wrapper itself and to fail closed, so correctness does not depend on every client shaping its body correctly.

tools.name: get_related
tools.title: Get related objects
tools.description: Reverse lookup: which objects reference this one. Use it to find pages to link to, and to check whether an object is safe to take offline or delete. This is relational usage data, not search, so it is exact rather than ranked. Do NOT use it to find textually similar content, that is find_similar.

permissions.scope: the object and every referencing object

cms.notes: All usage endpoints take id (repeatable), nodeId and the paging parameters skipCount, maxItems, sortby, sortorder. /page/usage/total and /file/usage/total return TotalUsageResponse, the others return PageUsageListResponse or the per-type list response. cms-mcp normalises them into one groups array.

tools.name: count_content
tools.title: Count and group content
tools.description: Counts matching objects, and optionally groups the count one way, without retrieving documents. Use it for reporting questions such as how many pages are offline, or how many per template. Counts are filtered by the acting user's permission groups but NOT by per-object permission, so they are an upper bound: when a number has to be exact, retrieve the objects with search_content and count what you received. CORPUS LIMIT: the same as search_content, only text an editor typed into a text part is indexed. Do NOT use this tool when you need the objects themselves. Counts run over the same indexed fields and object types search_content matches: a count_content call with a search's own inputs (query, types, nodeId, folderId, recursive, languages, filters) reproduces that search's total. queryUsed is returned for display and cannot be passed back to either tool.

composes: a match_all inside the query.bool wrapper so the filter is injected

permissions.scope: counted objects, enforced by the injected group filter

query.description: Omit to count everything in scope.

online.description: True for published objects only, false for offline only. Omit for both.

templateIds.description: Restrict to pages built on these templates.

editedAfter.description: Only objects edited at or after this Unix timestamp.

filters.description: The three supported filters, AND-combined and translated into bool.filter term and range clauses. Anything else has to be expressed through rawQuery.

groupBy.description: Group the count one way. Omit for a single total, which is the cheaper path.

totalIsExact.description: False whenever the total is a permission-group upper bound.

groups.description: Present only when groupBy was given.

cms.notes: Always sent with size: 0. Without groupBy the answer is hits.total and no aggregation is requested at all, which is the cheap path. With groupBy, exactly one terms aggregation is added: languageCode for language, templateId for template, online for online, sized by groupLimit. MANDATORY QUERY WRAPPING: cms-mcp MUST send every body to /rest/elastic shaped as {"query":{"bool":{"must":[<the actual query>],"filter":[]}}}, and MUST wrap a caller-supplied rawQuery the same way when it does not already carry query.bool. SearchResourceImpl.addFilters returns the body UNMODIFIED on three paths: no query key at all (so a bare {"size":0,"aggs":{...}} body is never filtered), a query without a bool key (the source carries a "// TODO add bool?" comment at that branch), and a bool.filter that is neither an object nor an array. On any of those paths NONE of the groupId terms filter, nodeId filter, folderId filter or wastebin filter is applied and only the per-hit canView post-filter remains. to be confirmed: Gentics should harden addFilters to create the bool wrapper itself and to fail closed, so correctness does not depend on every client shaping its body correctly. A bare {"size": 0, "aggs": {...}} body has no query key and would therefore be forwarded with NO permission filter, which is why the match_all wrapper is mandatory here. COUNT ACCURACY: the per-hit post-filter replaces hits.hits only and does NOT adjust hits.total, and aggregations are not post-filtered at all. Totals and aggregation counts therefore reflect the injected group-based filter, not the per-object canView check, and may overstate slightly where group permission and object permission diverge.

groups.title: Content read
groups.description: Reading the content tree and individual objects, and rendering a page preview. Retrieval finds candidates; these tools verify them.

tools.name: get_folder_tree
tools.title: Get folder tree
tools.description: Returns the folder structure of a node as a nested tree, so you can choose where a page belongs. Start at the node root by omitting folderId. Keep depth small: a deep tree of a real site will not fit in context. Do NOT use it to list pages or files, it returns folders only, use list_folder_items.

composes: depth trimming the CMS does not offer

includeCounts.description: Add pageCount per folder. Costs one extra CMS call per folder.

cms.notes: GET /folder/getFolders/{id} with tree=true, recursive=true, nodeId and wastebin=exclude returns LegacyFolderListResponse. The CMS has no depth parameter, so cms-mcp trims the returned tree to depth and sets hasMoreChildren on the cut nodes. includeCounts uses GET /folder/count/{id}, which returns FolderObjectCountResponse.

tools.name: list_folder_items
tools.title: List folder items
tools.description: Lists the pages, files, images, folders and forms in one folder, with edit and publish state. This is the exact inventory of a folder, unlike search_content which is ranked retrieval. Use it when the user names a folder, and to check whether a page already exists there before creating one.

cms.notes: GET /folder/getItems/{folderId} returns ItemListResponse and accepts type (repeatable), nodeId, recursive, language, langfallback, search, sortby, sortorder, skipCount, maxItems, online, modified, creatorId, editorId, createdbefore, createdsince, editedbefore, editedsince, publishedbefore, publishedsince. nameContains maps to search. MCP size/from map to maxItems/skipCount.

tools.name: get_page
tools.title: Get page
tools.description: Loads one page: properties, and with include tags, its content blocks and their values. This is the authoritative read: use it to verify exact wording before quoting a page, and to read a page back after writing it. It does NOT take an edit lock, so it is safe to call at any time and it will not block a human editor. Use render_preview if you need the rendered HTML rather than the tag values.

properties.description: Flattened partKeyword -> value, typed by part type.

propertiesRaw.description: Raw CMS Property objects, only when include contains constructs.

tags.description: Keyed by tag name, which is the CMS Tag.name.

page.description: Normalised CMS Page. Tag properties are flattened to partKeyword -> value; the raw CMS Property union is available under propertiesRaw on request.

cms.notes: GET /page/load/{id} returns PageLoadResponse and accepts update (MUST stay false here), template, folder, langvars, pagevars, workflow, translationstatus, versioninfo, disinherited, construct, nodeId. include maps: tags is implicit in the Page object, template -> template=true, folder -> folder=true, languageVariants -> langvars=true, versions -> versioninfo=true, translationStatus -> translationstatus=true, constructs -> construct=true plus propertiesRaw in the output.

tools.name: get_page_tags
tools.title: Get page tags
tools.description: Returns just the content blocks of a page, paged and searchable by tag name. Use it when a page has many tags and the full page object from get_page would be too large. Do NOT use it as the first read of an unknown page: it gives you no page properties and no template context.

cms.notes: GET /page/getTags/{id} returns TagListResponse with search, sort and paging parameters.

tools.name: list_templates
tools.title: List templates
tools.description: Lists the page templates a folder or node allows, with the fields a client needs to let a user choose one before a page is created. Scope it with folderId whenever the target folder is known: the result is then exactly the set create_page accepts for that folder. Use it to offer template options, and get_template to inspect one; it does not return template source.

nodeId.description: Restrict to the templates assigned to this node.

folderId.description: Restrict to the templates linked to this folder, the set create_page accepts there.

cms.notes: GET /template returns TemplateInNodeResponse with nodeId (repeatable), q, sort, page, pageSize, perms, inherited, checkPermission, reduce. Folder-scoped listing uses GET /folder/getTemplates/{folderId}; node-scoped GET /node/{nodeId}/templates.

tools.name: get_template
tools.title: Get template
tools.description: Loads a template and the tags it defines, including which of those tags a page may fill (editableInPage) and which are mandatory. Call this before building page content: it tells you the slots that exist. It does NOT tell you which constructs are available in the node, use list_constructs with nodeId for that.

includeSource.description: Include the raw template markup. Large; only request it when you must inspect the markup.

cms.notes: GET /template/load/{id}?nodeId= returns TemplateLoadResponse. Template carries source (raw markup with <node keyword> references), templateTags {name: TemplateTag} and objectTags. TemplateTag adds editableInPage and mandatory on top of the Tag shape. GET /template/{id}/tag returns TagList.

tools.name: get_file
tools.title: Get file
tools.description: Loads the metadata of one file: name, size, mime type, online state and URL. Use it to confirm a file exists and is published before linking to it. It does NOT return the binary content.

cms.notes: GET /file/load/{id} returns FileLoadResponse. Binary content is GET /file/content/load/{id} and is deliberately not exposed as a tool.

tools.name: get_image
tools.title: Get image
tools.description: Loads the metadata of one image, including pixel dimensions, so you can judge whether it suits a hero or teaser slot. It does NOT return the binary content and it does not resize anything.

cms.notes: GET /image/load/{id} returns ImageLoadResponse, which extends the file model with sizeX, sizeY, dpiX, dpiY and focal point fields.

tools.name: get_page_versions
tools.title: Get page versions
tools.description: Returns the version history of a page with editor and timestamp for each version, plus which version is current and which is published. Use it to answer who changed a page and when, and to choose a version for restore_page_version. It does NOT return the content of old versions.

cms.notes: GET /page/load/{id}?versioninfo=true populates Page.versions [PageVersion {number, timestamp, editor}], Page.currentVersion and Page.publishedVersion. There is no standalone versions endpoint.

tools.name: render_preview
tools.title: Render page preview
tools.description: Renders a saved page the way the CMS will publish it, and returns a preview URL plus optionally the HTML. Use it to check that content and constructs actually render, and give the URL to the user so they can look at the page. Request html only when you need to inspect the output yourself: rendered HTML is large. Preview covers pages only; there is no template or construct preview.

mode.description: edit renders with editable markers for the Aloha editor.

cms.notes: GET /page/render/{id} returns PageRenderResponse {content, inheritedContent, properties, tags, metaeditables, time} and accepts nodeId, template, edit, proxyprefix, links (backend|frontend), tagmap, inherited, publish, version. GET /devtools/preview/page/{id}?nodeId= returns raw text/html and is the cheaper source for html. To be confirmed: availability of the devtools preview route for a non-Editor-UI client, and the lifetime and auth model of previewUrl.

tools.name: get_publish_state
tools.title: Get publish state
tools.description: Returns the publish protocol: who published or unpublished an object and when. Use it when the user asks who put something online, where the indexed published timestamp is not enough. Not implemented in Phase One.

cms.notes: PublishProtocolResource, verified at cms-oss/cms-restapi/.../rest/resource/PublishProtocolResource.java. Returns PublishLogDto {objId, type, state, user, date} (record in .../rest/model/PublishLogDto.java); the list form takes PagingParameterBean plus FilterPublishableObjectBean {type, objId}.

groups.title: Content write
groups.description: The only mutation path for CMS content. Each tool acts on one object and completes its own lock cycle. Omitted from tools/list for users with no page create or edit permission in any node.

tools.name: create_page
tools.title: Create page
tools.description: Creates a new page as an OFFLINE draft in a folder, from a template. The page is never published by this tool; publishing is a separate, explicit step. Resolve folderId, templateId and language first (get_folder_tree, get_template, list_nodes) and check permission with get_permissions. Do NOT call it twice for the same page: with failOnDuplicate it errors on a duplicate filename instead of creating a second page.

idempotencyKey.description: Opaque client-supplied key. Phase One: logged, otherwise ignored. Reserved for server-side de-duplication.

properties.description: Flattened partKeyword -> value, typed by part type.

propertiesRaw.description: Raw CMS Property objects, only when include contains constructs.

tags.description: Keyed by tag name, which is the CMS Tag.name.

page.description: Normalised CMS Page. Tag properties are flattened to partKeyword -> value; the raw CMS Property union is available under propertiesRaw on request.

cms.notes: PageCreateRequest {folderId, templateId, variantId, variantChannelId, language, nodeId, pageName, description, priority, contentSetId, fileName, niceUrl, alternateUrls, forceExtension, failOnDuplicate}; response PageLoadResponse. MCP name maps to pageName, fileName to fileName. A created page is offline until publish_page is called.

tools.name: update_page_tags
tools.title: Update page tags
tools.description: Sets the values of one or more content blocks on a page in a single call. This is the only way to write page content. The tool takes the edit lock, applies exactly the values you give, saves, creates a version and releases the lock, so you never have to lock or unlock anything yourself. Values are written byte for byte: nothing is reformatted, re-encoded or reflowed, which is what makes verbatim text reproduction possible. Name only the tags and parts you want to change; untouched tags are left alone. Use add_page_tag first if a tag does not exist yet, or set createMissing with a constructKeyword. Do NOT use this tool for page metadata such as name or filename, that is update_page_properties.

constructKeyword.description: Required only when createMissing is true and the tag does not exist yet.

properties.description: partKeyword -> value. Strings for text and rich-text parts, booleans for checkboxes, integer ids for page, file, image and folder parts, arrays of strings for multi-selects.

tags.description: Keyed by tag name (CMS Tag.name), e.g. content or genaix_hero_1.

idempotencyKey.description: Opaque client-supplied key. Phase One: logged, otherwise ignored. Reserved for server-side de-duplication.

properties.description: Flattened partKeyword -> value, typed by part type.

propertiesRaw.description: Raw CMS Property objects, only when include contains constructs.

tags.description: Keyed by tag name, which is the CMS Tag.name.

page.description: Normalised CMS Page. Tag properties are flattened to partKeyword -> value; the raw CMS Property union is available under propertiesRaw on request.

cms.notes: Three CMS calls inside one transaction: GET /page/load/{id}?update=true to take the lock, optionally POST /page/newtags/{id} (MultiTagCreateRequest) for missing tags, then POST /page/save/{id} with PageSaveRequest {page, unlock: true, createVersion, delete}. The CMS has no patch-one-tag endpoint: the whole Page object must be round-tripped, which cms-mcp does internally. Values land in page.tags[name].properties[part] as CMS Property objects, with the populated field chosen by part type (stringValue, booleanValue, pageId, fileId, imageId, folderId, stringValues). MUST NOT normalise whitespace or re-encode entities.

tools.name: add_page_tag
tools.title: Add page tag
tools.description: Adds one new content block of a given construct to a page and returns its generated tag name, which you then fill with update_page_tags. Check with list_constructs that the construct is available in the page's node first. Calling this twice adds two blocks, so do not retry it blindly after a timeout: read the page with get_page_tags instead. Pass exactly one of constructKeyword or constructId; a call with neither or both is refused as invalid-params.

tagName.description: Optional explicit name. Omit to let the CMS generate one.

copyFrom.description: Copy the values of an existing tag from another page.

idempotencyKey.description: Opaque client-supplied key. Phase One: logged, otherwise ignored. Reserved for server-side de-duplication.

inputRule.note: Exactly one of these members must be present. Enforced by the server with invalid-params; kept out of inputSchema because a root-level anyOf/oneOf is not accepted by every MCP host that hands tool schemas to a model.

cms.notes: POST /page/newtag/{id}?constructId=|keyword= with ContentTagCreateRequest {magicValue, constructId, keyword, copyPageId, copyTagname} returns TagCreateResponse {tag}. POST /page/newtags/{id} with MultiTagCreateRequest creates several at once; cms-mcp uses it internally for update_page_tags createMissing.

tools.name: update_page_properties
tools.title: Update page properties
tools.description: Changes page metadata: name, filename, description, nice URL, priority or template. Content blocks are untouched. Changing templateId can orphan content that the new template has no slot for, so read get_template for both templates before doing it. Do NOT use this tool to change content, that is update_page_tags.

idempotencyKey.description: Opaque client-supplied key. Phase One: logged, otherwise ignored. Reserved for server-side de-duplication.

properties.description: Flattened partKeyword -> value, typed by part type.

propertiesRaw.description: Raw CMS Property objects, only when include contains constructs.

tags.description: Keyed by tag name, which is the CMS Tag.name.

page.description: Normalised CMS Page. Tag properties are flattened to partKeyword -> value; the raw CMS Property union is available under propertiesRaw on request.

cms.notes: Same lock cycle as update_page_tags: GET /page/load/{id}?update=true then POST /page/save/{id} with PageSaveRequest {page, unlock: true, deriveFileName, failOnDuplicate}. Only the named fields are modified on the loaded Page.

tools.name: publish_page
tools.title: Publish page
tools.description: Publishes a page now, or schedules it for a timestamp. The CMS decides from the acting user's permissions and the configured workflow whether the page goes online directly or enters the approval queue, so ALWAYS read result from the response and tell the user which happened: never report a page as live when result is queued_for_approval. Check publish permission with get_permissions first, and verify the content with render_preview before publishing. There is no separate review-request tool: when the acting user lacks publishpages on the folder, this call queues the page for approval and reports it; a review request by a user who may publish directly is a client-side workflow step, not a CMS call.

composes: GET /page/pubqueue, to tell published from queued for approval

message.description: Note for the approval queue, shown to the approver.

idempotencyKey.description: Opaque client-supplied key. Phase One: logged, otherwise ignored. Reserved for server-side de-duplication.

cms.notes: POST /page/publish/{id}?nodeId= with PagePublishRequest {message, alllang, at, keepVersion} returns GenericResponse only, so cms-mcp MUST read the resulting state back to fill result and approval: GET /page/load/{id}?workflow=true populates Page.workflow {groups, message, user, modified, timestamp} and Page.online/queued/planned. GET /page/pubqueue lists pages awaiting approval. To be confirmed: whether a cheaper signal exists.

tools.name: take_offline
tools.title: Take page offline
tools.description: Unpublishes a page immediately or at a timestamp. The page and its content remain in the CMS; only the published version is withdrawn. Check with get_related that nothing important links to the page before you do this. It is not a delete, use delete_page for that.

idempotencyKey.description: Opaque client-supplied key. Phase One: logged, otherwise ignored. Reserved for server-side de-duplication.

cms.notes: POST /page/takeOffline/{id} with PageOfflineRequest {alllang, at} returns GenericResponse. Idempotent: taking an offline page offline is a no-op.

tools.name: delete_page
tools.title: Delete page to wastebin
tools.description: Moves a page to the wastebin, where it remains restorable by a human in the CMS. It is not a permanent delete and this tool cannot purge anything. Confirm with the user before calling it, and check get_related first: other pages may link to this one.

cms.notes: POST /page/delete/{id} moves the page to the wastebin and returns GenericResponse. The purge route POST /page/wastebin/delete/{id} is deliberately NOT exposed.

tools.name: translate_page
tools.title: Create language variant
tools.description: Creates the language variant of a page, or opens the existing one, as the starting point for a translation. It copies the source content into the new language variant; it does not translate anything. Write the translated text afterwards with update_page_tags. Check list_nodes that the node actually supports the target language.

idempotencyKey.description: Opaque client-supplied key. Phase One: logged, otherwise ignored. Reserved for server-side de-duplication.

properties.description: Flattened partKeyword -> value, typed by part type.

propertiesRaw.description: Raw CMS Property objects, only when include contains constructs.

tags.description: Keyed by tag name, which is the CMS Tag.name.

page.description: Normalised CMS Page. Tag properties are flattened to partKeyword -> value; the raw CMS Property union is available under propertiesRaw on request.

cms.notes: POST /page/translate/{id}?language=&locked=&channelId= returns PageLoadResponse for the language variant. Calling it again for an existing variant returns that variant, so the tool is idempotent.

tools.name: restore_page_version
tools.title: Restore page version
tools.description: Restores a previous version of a page, making it the current version. Always list the versions with get_page_versions first and confirm the target version with the user: this overwrites the current content. Restoring does not publish; call publish_page afterwards if the page should go live.

version.description: Version timestamp, as returned by get_page_versions.

idempotencyKey.description: Opaque client-supplied key. Phase One: logged, otherwise ignored. Reserved for server-side de-duplication.

properties.description: Flattened partKeyword -> value, typed by part type.

propertiesRaw.description: Raw CMS Property objects, only when include contains constructs.

tags.description: Keyed by tag name, which is the CMS Tag.name.

page.description: Normalised CMS Page. Tag properties are flattened to partKeyword -> value; the raw CMS Property union is available under propertiesRaw on request.

cms.notes: POST /page/restore/{id}?version= returns PageLoadResponse. POST /page/restore/{pageid}/{tag} restores a single tag and is not exposed in Phase One.

tools.name: upload_file
tools.title: Upload file or image
tools.description: Puts a binary into a CMS folder so a page can reference it. Prefer source.kind url, where the server fetches the file: base64 is capped at 5 MB because it travels inside the tool call. Use the node's default file or image folder from list_nodes unless the user names a folder. This tool does not resize or convert anything.

data.description: Base64 payload, at most 5 MB decoded.

url.description: HTTPS URL the server fetches. Must be on the allowlist configured for the calling installation.

idempotencyKey.description: Opaque client-supplied key. Phase One: logged, otherwise ignored. Reserved for server-side de-duplication.

cms.notes: POST /file/createSimple?folderId=&nodeId=&description=&overwrite= takes multipart/form-data and returns FileUploadResponse; POST /file/create takes a MultiPart body. MCP has no binary channel, so cms-mcp decodes base64 or fetches the URL server-side and builds the multipart request itself. Images are stored through the same route and recognised by mime type. To be confirmed: whether an outbound server-side fetch is permitted, and should it be host-allowlisted per installation token? Recommendation: HTTPS only, allowlist, 25 MB cap, no redirects.

groups.title: Constructs and devtools packages
groups.description: Tier 1 Handlebars construct authoring. Omitted from tools/list for users without the updateconstructs permission. Group roles summarise the tools' roles: the read tools (list_constructs, get_construct, list_construct_categories, list_part_types, list_datasources, get_datasource) are listed for any user whose type-level permissions include construct view, which a content creator holds; the write tools need updateconstructs. A read-only allowlist, such as a quality gate's or a reviewer agent's, may name the read tools of this group by their access and never its writes.

tools.name: list_constructs
tools.title: List constructs
tools.description: Lists the constructs (tag types) available, filtered by node or by the page they could be inserted into. ALWAYS call this before creating a construct, to check that the keyword is free and that no existing construct already does the job, and before building page content, to see what you are allowed to use. Filtering by nodeId or pageId is what tells you availability: a construct that exists in the CMS is not necessarily assigned to the node you are working in.

changeable.description: Only constructs the acting user may change.

cms.notes: GET /construct returns PagedConstructListResponse and accepts q, sort, page, pageSize, changeable, pageId, nodeId, category, partTypeId (repeatable), perms, embed=category. GET /node/{nodeId}/constructs takes the same filters and is the node-scoped variant.

tools.name: get_construct
tools.title: Get construct
tools.description: Loads one construct in full, including every part and the Handlebars template source. This is the mandatory first step before update_construct, because an update replaces the whole part list and you need to know what is there. The template is returned under template, not among parts: REST reports its type as RICHTEXT, so you cannot identify it by type alone. Pass exactly one of id or keyword; a call with neither or both is refused as invalid-params.

inputRule.note: Exactly one of these members must be present. Enforced by the server with invalid-params; kept out of inputSchema because a root-level anyOf/oneOf is not accepted by every MCP host that hands tool schemas to a model.

template.description: The Handlebars part, surfaced separately so it is not mistaken for a rich-text content part. REST reports its Property.type as RICHTEXT.

cms.notes: GET /construct/{id}?embed=category returns ConstructLoadResponse {construct}. Resolving by keyword needs GET /construct?q=<keyword> first, since the CMS has no load-by-keyword route. GET /construct/{id}/nodes returns NodeList for nodeRefs. The Handlebars part is the part with typeId 43; its template is in defaultProperty.stringValue.

tools.name: create_construct
tools.title: Create Tier 1 Handlebars construct
tools.description: Creates a new construct with a Handlebars template and editable parts, and assigns it to the given nodes, in one CMS transaction. Pass the template as plain Handlebars source in handlebarsTemplate: the server creates the type-43 template part itself, so never describe that part in parts. nodeIds is required; the CMS rejects a create without it. Before calling: check the keyword is free with list_constructs, resolve the category with ensure_construct_category, discover which part types this installation allows with list_part_types, and validate the template syntax client-side, because the CMS will accept a broken template and only fail at render time. Afterwards, prove it renders by inserting it into a page and calling render_preview. This tool creates Tier 1 constructs only, meaning ones that render into page content. It cannot create structured fields that need a content-repository mapping.

composes: synthesises the whole Construct body including the Handlebars part at typeId 43
POST /construct?nodeId= which also links the nodes

keyword.description: Unique machine name, also the tag type name in the editor.

name.description: Language code -> text, e.g. {"de": "Hallo Box", "en": "Hello box"}. Always supply at least de and en for the showcase.

handlebarsTemplate.description: Handlebars source. Access part values as cms.tag.parts.<partKeyword> (for example {{cms.tag.parts.headline}}); the shorter tag.parts.<keyword> and a bare {{keyword}} do not resolve in the CMS Handlebars part type.

keyword.description: Machine name used in the Handlebars template as cms.tag.parts.<keyword>.

name.description: Language code -> text, e.g. {"de": "Hallo Box", "en": "Hello box"}. Always supply at least de and en for the showcase.

typeId.description: CMS part type id. Call list_part_types first and use an id it reports with allowedForGeneratedConstructs true: the set is an installation-level allowlist, not a fixed list, and the CMS rejects anything outside it with a validation problem. Type id 43 is always rejected here, because the Handlebars template goes into handlebarsTemplate rather than into a part.

datasourceId.description: Required when typeId is 29 (single select) or 30 (multi select), and rejected otherwise: a select part draws its options from a datasource. Find one with list_datasources and inspect its entries with get_datasource. Datasources cannot be created through this server in Phase One.

defaultValue.description: Initial value. Lands in defaultProperty, typed by the part type.

parts.description: Editable parts. Do NOT include the Handlebars template part here.

allowExisting.description: When the keyword already exists: false errors, true returns the existing construct with created false.

idempotencyKey.description: Opaque client-supplied key. Phase One: logged, otherwise ignored. Reserved for server-side de-duplication.

template.description: The Handlebars part, surfaced separately so it is not mistaken for a rich-text content part. REST reports its Property.type as RICHTEXT.

cms.notes: POST /construct?nodeId=<id>[&nodeId=...] with a full Construct body creates the construct, its parts and the node links in one transaction; ConstructResourceImpl.create throws MissingFieldException("nodeId") when the query parameter is missing, then loops the ids calling node.addConstruct. cms-mcp builds the Handlebars part itself: {keyword: templatePartKeyword, typeId: 43, editable: false, partOrder: 1, defaultProperty: {type: "RICHTEXT", stringValue: handlebarsTemplate}}. typeId 43 is the HandlebarsPartType, verified at cms-oss/cms-restapi/.../rest/model/Property.java:55 (case 43: // Handlebars -> RICHTEXT) and cms-oss/cms-core/.../object/parttype/handlebars/HandlebarsPartType.java; there is no HANDLEBARS literal in the REST Property.type enum. id and globalId must be omitted for new constructs. categoryId must already exist, the REST path does not resolve a category by name.

tools.name: update_construct
tools.title: Update construct
tools.description: Changes an existing construct. The CMS replaces the whole part list on update, so this tool reads the construct first and merges your changes over it: supply only what you want changed. If you do pass parts, it must be the COMPLETE desired list, because anything omitted is deleted, and part type ids come from list_part_types. Passing nodeIds sets the exact node assignment, adding and removing as needed; omit it to leave assignments alone. Existing pages keep content for parts you delete but can no longer edit it, so prefer adding parts over renaming or removing them. Pass exactly one of id or keyword; a call with neither or both is refused as invalid-params.

name.description: Language code -> text, e.g. {"de": "Hallo Box", "en": "Hello box"}. Always supply at least de and en for the showcase.

handlebarsTemplate.description: Handlebars source. Access part values as cms.tag.parts.<partKeyword> (for example {{cms.tag.parts.headline}}); the shorter tag.parts.<keyword> and a bare {{keyword}} do not resolve in the CMS Handlebars part type.

keyword.description: Machine name used in the Handlebars template as cms.tag.parts.<keyword>.

name.description: Language code -> text, e.g. {"de": "Hallo Box", "en": "Hello box"}. Always supply at least de and en for the showcase.

typeId.description: CMS part type id. Call list_part_types first and use an id it reports with allowedForGeneratedConstructs true: the set is an installation-level allowlist, not a fixed list, and the CMS rejects anything outside it with a validation problem. Type id 43 is always rejected here, because the Handlebars template goes into handlebarsTemplate rather than into a part.

datasourceId.description: Required when typeId is 29 (single select) or 30 (multi select), and rejected otherwise: a select part draws its options from a datasource. Find one with list_datasources and inspect its entries with get_datasource. Datasources cannot be created through this server in Phase One.

defaultValue.description: Initial value. Lands in defaultProperty, typed by the part type.

parts.description: COMPLETE replacement list of editable parts. Omit to keep the current parts.

nodeIds.description: Desired-state node assignment. Omit to leave it untouched.

idempotencyKey.description: Opaque client-supplied key. Phase One: logged, otherwise ignored. Reserved for server-side de-duplication.

inputRule.note: Exactly one of these members must be present. Enforced by the server with invalid-params; kept out of inputSchema because a root-level anyOf/oneOf is not accepted by every MCP host that hands tool schemas to a model.

template.description: The Handlebars part, surfaced separately so it is not mistaken for a rich-text content part. REST reports its Property.type as RICHTEXT.

cms.notes: GET /construct/{id} then PUT /construct/{id}?nodeId=... with the merged Construct body. Construct.REST2NODE clears parts and rebuilds the list, matching by globalId where present, so there is no partial update; cms-mcp preserves each kept part's globalId from the read so ids stay stable. On update the nodeId list is a desired-state list that ConstructResourceImpl.update diffs with addConstruct and removeConstruct. Known limitation: read-merge-write races if two clients update the same construct; a patch-style endpoint would remove the race.

tools.name: ensure_construct_category
tools.title: Ensure construct category
tools.description: Returns the id of a construct category with the given name, creating the category if it does not exist. Needed because create_construct takes a category id and the CMS REST path cannot resolve a category by name. Call list_construct_categories first if you would rather reuse an existing category under a different name.

name.description: Language code -> text, e.g. {"de": "Hallo Box", "en": "Hello box"}. Always supply at least de and en for the showcase.

idempotencyKey.description: Opaque client-supplied key. Phase One: logged, otherwise ignored. Reserved for server-side de-duplication.

cms.notes: GET /construct/category lists ConstructCategory {id, globalId, name, nameI18n, sortOrder}; POST /construct/category creates one. Matching is on the name in any supplied language, case-insensitive. Idempotent.

tools.name: list_construct_categories
tools.title: List construct categories
tools.description: Lists the construct categories, which group tag types in the editor's insert menu. Use it to pick an existing category before falling back to ensure_construct_category.

cms.notes: GET /construct/category returns the category list. ConstructCategory.constructs is a map of Construct objects which cms-mcp reduces to a count.

tools.name: assign_construct_to_nodes
tools.title: Assign constructs to nodes
tools.description: Sets, adds or removes the nodes in which constructs are available. Use mode set to make the given node list the exact assignment, add to extend it, remove to withdraw. A construct not assigned to a node cannot be inserted into pages of that node, which is the usual reason a construct seems to be missing.

idempotencyKey.description: Opaque client-supplied key. Phase One: logged, otherwise ignored. Reserved for server-side de-duplication.

cms.notes: POST /construct/link/nodes and /construct/unlink/nodes take BulkLinkUpdateRequest {ids: construct ids, targetIds: node ids}. mode set is implemented as read current assignment via GET /construct/{id}/nodes, then link the additions and unlink the removals. The single-pair routes PUT and DELETE /node/{nodeId}/constructs/{constructId} are the fallback.

tools.name: add_construct_to_package
tools.title: Add construct to devtools package
tools.description: Adds an existing construct to a devtools package so it becomes version-controllable and promotable between environments. This only records membership: it does not write any file and does not synchronise anything. A human runs the filesystem synchronisation, which is deliberately not available as a tool. Pass exactly one of constructId or constructKeyword; a call with neither or both is refused as invalid-params.

idempotencyKey.description: Opaque client-supplied key. Phase One: logged, otherwise ignored. Reserved for server-side de-duplication.

inputRule.note: Exactly one of these members must be present. Enforced by the server with invalid-params; kept out of inputSchema because a root-level anyOf/oneOf is not accepted by every MCP host that hands tool schemas to a model.

cms.notes: PUT /devtools/packages/{name}/constructs/{construct} with an empty body adds the construct to the package; {construct} accepts an id, a keyword or a globalId. The sync routes PUT /devtools/packages/{name}/cms2fs and fs2cms are deliberately NOT exposed.

tools.name: list_packages
tools.title: List devtools packages
tools.description: Lists the devtools packages, so you can pick a target for add_construct_to_package. Packages are bundles of constructs, templates and other definitions used to promote work between environments.

cms.notes: GET /devtools/packages returns PackageListResponse with q, sort, page, pageSize. Package carries per-type counts and subPackages.

tools.name: list_part_types
tools.title: List part types
tools.description: Lists the part types installed in this CMS, and which of them may be used in a construct created through this server. ALWAYS call this before create_construct or update_construct and pick type ids it reports with allowedForGeneratedConstructs true: the allowed set is installation configuration, not a fixed list, so a hard-coded id may be rejected. Type id 43 never appears as allowed, because the Handlebars template goes into create_construct's handlebarsTemplate rather than into a part. Do NOT use this tool to discover the parts of an existing construct, that is get_construct.

allowedOnly.description: Return only the part types allowed for generated constructs.

cms.notes: GET /parttype returns an array of PartType {id, name, description, auto, javaClass, deprecated} and takes a q filter. The REST model carries NO keyword field, so a part type is identified by its numeric id. allowedForGeneratedConstructs, requiresDatasource and note are added by cms-mcp from the installation-level allowlist; they are not CMS fields. The allowlist default is the 15 Tier 1 ids 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 9, 10, 21, 25, 29, 30, 31, 38, 39; 29 and 30 set requiresDatasource. 43 is excluded because the template is not a part input, and 13 (overview), 32 (datasource), 33 (Velocity), 34 (breadcrumb), 35 (navigation) and the form types 41 and 42 are excluded in Phase One because they need settings this surface does not model or imply Tier 2 work.

tools.name: list_datasources
tools.title: List datasources
tools.description: Lists the datasources in this CMS. A datasource supplies the options of a select part, so call this to find the datasourceId a select part needs (type id 29 or 30) before create_construct. Datasources cannot be created or changed through this server; if none fits, that is a task for a human in the CMS.

cms.notes: GET /datasource returns PagedDatasourceListResponse and takes q, sort, page, pageSize. Datasource is {id, globalId, type: STATIC|SITEMINDER, name}; entryCount is filled by cms-mcp from GET /datasource/{id}/entries where cheap, and omitted otherwise.

tools.name: get_datasource
tools.title: Get datasource
tools.description: Loads one datasource with its entries, so you can see the option keys and values a select part built on it will offer. Use it to check that a datasource actually contains the options the construct needs before wiring a select part to it.

cms.notes: GET /datasource/{id} returns DatasourceLoadResponse and GET /datasource/{id}/entries returns DatasourceEntryListResponse with DatasourceEntryModel {id, globalId, dsId, key, value}. GET /datasource/{id}/constructs lists the constructs already using it and fills constructRefs.

tools.name: request_tier2_field_mapping
tools.title: Request Tier 2 field mapping
tools.description: Records the request to map a construct part to a content-repository field, which is what a structured Tier 2 construct needs. NOT implemented in Phase One and deliberately human-gated: it would create the tagmap entry but never trigger the content-repository structure repair, because that is a long-running schema migration against a live repository. It returns a human-actionable next step, not a finished mapping. Do not present a Tier 2 construct as usable on the strength of this call.

idempotencyKey.description: Opaque client-supplied key. Phase One: logged, otherwise ignored. Reserved for server-side de-duplication.

cms.notes: Would create a TagmapEntryModel via POST /contentrepositories/{id}/entries. It MUST NOT call PUT /contentrepositories/{id}/structure/repair or .../data/repair. To be confirmed: the right route for a tagmap entry and the supported human repair procedure.

groups.title: User and group administration
groups.description: Scenario S4, which is optional. Omitted from tools/list for users without createuser and updategroupuser. No tool writes permission bits.

tools.name: list_users
tools.title: List users
tools.description: Finds CMS users by name, login or email. Call it before create_user to check whether the person already has an account, which is the common case in an existing installation.
