cms.notes: GET /user returns UserList with q, sort, page, pageSize, perms, embed. The password field of User is never returned by this tool. includeGroups uses embed or GET /user/{id}/groups.

tools.name: list_groups
tools.title: List groups
tools.description: Lists the CMS groups. Groups carry the permissions that make up a role, so this is how you find the group that corresponds to a role the user names. Group names alone do not prove what a group may do: confirm with get_group_permissions.

cms.notes: GET /group returns GroupList with q, sort, page, pageSize, perms; Group is {id, name, description} only, so memberCount needs GET /group/{id}/users and is best effort.

tools.name: get_group_permissions
tools.title: Get group permissions
tools.description: Returns what a group may do, either on an object type or on one specific object, as a list of named permissions with labels. This is the read a permission impact preview is built from. It describes a GROUP, not a user: a user's effective rights are the union over their groups, which is what preview_permission_impact computes.

cms.notes: Returns TypePermissionResponse {perms: [TypePermissionItem {type, label, description, category, value, editable}], roles: [RoleItem]}. The MCP field granted carries TypePermissionItem.value and name carries its type. The write counterparts POST /group/{id}/perms/... are deliberately NOT exposed.

tools.name: create_user
tools.title: Create user in group
tools.description: Creates a CMS user and places them in a group in the same call. groupId is REQUIRED: the CMS has no standalone user-create endpoint, so there is no way to create a user without a group. Check with list_users that the login is free, and with get_group_permissions that the group carries the intended role. Always show preview_permission_impact to the user and get their confirmation before calling this.

password.description: Omit where the installation provisions credentials externally, for example via single sign-on.

idempotencyKey.description: Opaque client-supplied key. Phase One: logged, otherwise ignored. Reserved for server-side de-duplication.

cms.notes: PUT /group/{id}/users with a User body {login, firstName, lastName, email, password, description} creates the user and adds them to the group, returning UserLoadResponse. Verified in cms-oss/cms-restapi/.../rest/resource/GroupResource.java (createUser, @PUT @Path("/{id}/users")). There is no POST /user. PUT /user/{id} is an update and DELETE /user/{id} deactivates rather than deletes, and neither is exposed.

tools.name: assign_user_to_group
tools.title: Assign user to group
tools.description: Adds an existing user to a group, which is how a role is granted. Optionally restrict the membership to specific nodes. Show preview_permission_impact first and get confirmation: this changes what the person can do immediately.

nodeIds.description: Restrict the membership to these nodes. Omit for all nodes.

idempotencyKey.description: Opaque client-supplied key. Phase One: logged, otherwise ignored. Reserved for server-side de-duplication.

cms.notes: PUT /user/{id}/groups/{groupId} adds the membership; PUT /user/{id}/groups/{groupId}/nodes/{nodeId} scopes it per node. Read back with GET /user/{id}/groups. Idempotent.

tools.name: remove_user_from_group
tools.title: Remove user from group
tools.description: Removes a user from a group, revoking the rights that group carried. Show preview_permission_impact first: the person may lose access to work in progress. Removing the last group of a user leaves them able to log in with no permissions.

idempotencyKey.description: Opaque client-supplied key. Phase One: logged, otherwise ignored. Reserved for server-side de-duplication.

cms.notes: DELETE /user/{id}/groups/{groupId} returns GenericResponse. Idempotent.

tools.name: preview_permission_impact
tools.title: Preview permission impact
tools.description: Shows what a user will and will not be able to do if the listed groups are added or removed, WITHOUT changing anything. Always run this and show the result before create_user, assign_user_to_group or remove_user_from_group. It is a composition of the group permissions the user would hold, not a CMS simulation: it does not reproduce folder-tree inheritance or every role and language subtlety, so present it as a preview and read the warnings it returns.

composes: unioned into a before and after view

cms.notes: No CMS simulation endpoint exists: the permission surface is read or written, never evaluated hypothetically. cms-mcp reads the user's current groups, reads each group's TypePermissionResponse for the requested types, and unions the result for the before and after sets. This is an approximation; the output carries warnings and computedBy composition. to be confirmed: whether a real POST /perm/simulate is worth adding. Recommendation: composition for Phase One.

groups.title: Design Studio (future)
groups.description: Template-level tools reserved for Design Studio. No tool in this group ships in Phase One; the group exists so the extension has a defined shape. list_templates moved to content_read in 1.0.0-rc.2.

tools.name: create_template
tools.title: Create template
tools.description: Creates a page template from raw markup and links it to folders. Phase-future: template changes affect every page using the template, so this needs the render_diff safeguard and an explicit human gate.

source.description: Raw template markup with <node keyword> tag references.

idempotencyKey.description: Opaque client-supplied key. Phase One: logged, otherwise ignored. Reserved for server-side de-duplication.

cms.notes: POST /template with TemplateCreateRequest {nodeId, folderIds, template: Template}; Template.source is the raw markup and templateTags is a {name: TemplateTag} map.

tools.name: update_template
tools.title: Update template
tools.description: Changes a template's markup or tags and optionally synchronises the pages using it. Phase-future and high blast radius: run render_diff on a sample of affected pages first.

idempotencyKey.description: Opaque client-supplied key. Phase One: logged, otherwise ignored. Reserved for server-side de-duplication.

cms.notes: POST /template/{id} with TemplateSaveRequest {template, unlock, syncPages, sync, forceSync, delete}. GET /template/{id}/tagstatus reports which pages fall out of sync after the change.

tools.name: link_template_to_folders
tools.title: Link template to folders
tools.description: Makes a template available in the given folders, so pages created there can use it, or withdraws it again with mode remove. A template that is not linked to a folder cannot be chosen when creating a page in that folder, which is the usual reason a template seems to be missing. Phase-future, part of the Design Studio group.

idempotencyKey.description: Opaque client-supplied key. Phase One: logged, otherwise ignored. Reserved for server-side de-duplication.

cms.notes: POST /template/link and /template/unlink take MultiLinkRequest; the single-template variants are POST /template/link/{id} and /template/unlink/{id} with LinkRequest.

tools.name: render_diff
tools.title: Diff rendered output
tools.description: Renders a page before and after a pending change and returns the difference, so a template or construct change can be proven not to alter unrelated pages. Phase-future; this is the safeguard that makes template editing safe enough to automate.

cms.notes: GET /page/diff/versions/{id} diffs two versions of a page; POST /diff/html and POST /diff/source are generic diff utilities; POST /page/preview renders an unsaved Page so a pending template can be previewed without saving it.

tools.name: decompose_design
tools.title: Decompose a design into template and constructs
tools.description: Placeholder for the Design Studio flow that turns a supplied HTML design into one template plus a set of constructs. Phase-future and client-side planning: its outputs are create_construct, create_template and link_template_to_folders, so no new CMS endpoint is needed beyond template creation. Not callable in Phase One.

composes: client-side planning with no CMS endpoint; its outputs are create_construct, create_template and link_template_to_folders

cms.notes: No CMS endpoint. Specification placeholder so the Design Studio extension has a named slot in this contract; the work is client-side planning whose outputs are existing write tools.

ObjectRef.title: ObjectRef
ObjectRef.description: Canonical reference to one CMS object, used in every tool in both directions. On output, type, id and name are always populated; nodeId is populated for every object below a node; globalId, path, language, niceUrl and url are best effort. On input, only type and id are read, so a ref received from another tool can be passed back unchanged without trimming it.

globalId.description: Cross-installation stable id (UUID-like), where the CMS has one.

path.description: Folder path of the object, e.g. /News/2026/.

language.description: Language code, pages and forms only.

niceUrl.description: The object's public path (nice URL), when the CMS has one.

url.description: The object's preview or published URL as the CMS would open it, when known. A client that needs one link takes url, then niceUrl, then path.

Problem.title: Problem
Problem.description: Error payload returned in structuredContent.problem when a tool call fails. The MCP result carries isError: true. Authentication failures never reach this shape: they are answered as HTTP 401 by the transport, before the MCP envelope.

detail.description: One sentence, i18n where the CMS supplies a message. Never a stack trace.
